q: 1. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient uphill side, involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: When the actual ground rises above (uphill of) the proposed contour gradient line, material must be excavated from the centre line to bring the road to the designed level.

q: 2. Two hill tops A and B 20 km apart are intervened by a third top C. If the top most contour of the three hill tops are of the same value, state whether the line of sight AB
options: passes below the hill top C
passes below the hill top C
explain: If all three hill tops have the same elevation, and C lies between A and B, the line of sight AB just touches (grazes) hill top C due to the curvature of the earth affecting the intermediate point differently.

q: 3. An imaginary line joining the points of equal elevation on the surface of the earth represents
explain: By definition, a contour line is the imaginary line on the ground joining points of equal elevation.

q: 4. The direction of steepest slope on the contour, is
options: at an angle of 45 deg to the contour
at right angles to the contour
explain: The steepest slope at any point on the ground is always along the line perpendicular (at right angles) to the contour at that point, since contours represent equal elevation.

q: 5. Two contour lines, having the same elevation
explain: Two contours of the same elevation can unite/merge together, for example in the case of a vertical cliff, where multiple contour lines coincide at a single line on the map.

q: 6. The angle of intersection of a contour and a ridge line, is
explain: A ridge line runs along the line of steepest ascent, and since contours are always perpendicular to the direction of steepest slope, a contour crosses a ridge (or valley) line at right angles (90 deg).

q: 7. A contour map of the area is essential before proceeding with the construction of
explain: For a large-scale earthwork project like a dam, a detailed contour map of the area is essential to plan the reservoir capacity, spillway location, and earthwork volumes.

q: 8. Contour lines
explain: Since a contour represents a closed line of constant elevation, every contour must eventually close upon itself, either within the map sheet or outside its boundary; it cannot simply end abruptly.

q: 9. Direct method of contouring is
explain: The direct method of contouring, where points actually lying on the contour are located and marked in the field, is the most accurate method, though it is slower than indirect methods.

q: 10. The angle of intersection of a counter and a ridge line, is
explain: Contour lines always cross ridge or valley lines at right angles (90 degrees), since ridge/valley lines represent the direction of steepest slope, which is perpendicular to the contour.

q: 11. In case of double line river, contours are
options: stopped at the banks of the river
stopped at the edge of the river
drawn by parabolic curves having their vertex at the centre of the water
explain: For a double line (wide) river, contours are shown stopping at the edge/bank of the river rather than being drawn across the water body.

q: 12. The contours merge or cross one another on the map in case of
explain: Contours merge (coincide) at a vertical cliff surface, and actually cross one another only in the special case of overhanging ground/caves, so all these listed conditions represent exceptions to the normal rule.

q: 13. Contour lines look to cross each other in case of
explain: Only in the special case of an overhanging cliff can contour lines appear to cross each other in plan view, since one part of the ground overhangs another at a different elevation but same horizontal projection.

q: 14. Closed contours with higher value inside represents a
explain: When the innermost closed contour has the highest elevation value, it represents a hill (elevated feature).

q: 15. When several contours coincide, it indicates
explain: When multiple contour lines of different elevations coincide (appear as a single line) on a map, it indicates a vertical cliff, where elevation changes without any horizontal distance.

q: 16. The contour interval depends upon the
explain: The choice of contour interval depends on multiple factors together: the nature/relief of the terrain, the scale of the map, and the purpose and extent of the survey.

q: 17. The vertical distance between the elevations represented by adjacent contour lines on a map is called
explain: As defined before, the constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours on a map is the contour interval.

q: 18. In route surveys, the most suitable method of contouring is
explain: For a linear route survey (road, railway, canal), contouring by cross-sections taken perpendicular to the centre line at regular intervals is the most suitable method.

q: 19. The spacing of cross-sections in a hilly country is usually
explain: In hilly terrain, where the ground changes rapidly, cross-sections for contouring/earthwork are usually spaced closer together than in flat country, but as per this text the given standard spacing is taken as 20 m.

q: 20. The contour interval is kept inversely proportional to
options: time and expense of field work
steepness of the configuration of the area
explain: Contour interval selection is influenced by multiple inversely related factors together - available time/budget, steepness of terrain, and map scale - so all of the above apply.

q: 21. The representation of general topography of a very flat terrain is possible only
options: by drawing contours at large interval
by drawing contours at small interval
by giving spot levels at large interval
by giving spot levels to features at close interval
explain: For very flat terrain, contours (even at a small interval) would be too widely spaced or non-existent to show relief adequately, so spot levels given at close intervals to features are needed instead.

q: 22. Contour interval, within the limits of a map
options: may vary according to the configuration
explain: Within a single map, the contour interval must be kept constant throughout, so that the spacing of contours consistently reflects the actual ground slope.

q: 23. The direction of steepest slope on a contour, is
options: at an angle of 45 to the contour
at right angles to the contour
explain: The direction of steepest slope at any point on a contour is always perpendicular (at right angles) to that contour line.

q: 24. Closed contours of decreasing values toward their centre, represent
explain: When closed contour loops show decreasing elevation values toward the centre, they represent a depression (low point), as opposed to a hill where values increase toward the centre.

q: 25. The horizontal equivalent which is a term generally uses in contoured map is
options: the least distance between two consecutive contours
the greatest distance between two consecutive contours
the mean distance between two consecutive contours
explain: As per the book's answer key, the horizontal equivalent in a contoured map is generally taken as the mean distance between two consecutive contours (representing the average ground slope over that interval).

q: 26. Which one of the following methods can be used for contour interpolation?
explain: Contour interpolation between plotted spot levels can be performed using any of several methods - estimation, arithmetical calculation, or graphical means - so all of these are valid approaches.

q: 27. In direct method of contouring, the process of locating or identifying points lying on a contour is called
explain: In the direct method of contouring, the process of locating points that lie exactly on a particular contour in the field is called ranging (tracing the contour).
